treaty_name: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the Republic of Lithuania for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income and on capital (2011; modified by MLI)
eif_quote: [Notification No. 28/2012, dated 25-7-2012] ... the date of entry into force of the said Agreement is the 10th July, 2012 ... sub-paragraph (a) of paragraph 3 of Article 31 of the said Agreement provides that the provisions of the said Agreement shall have effect in India in respect of taxes withheld at source, on income derived on or after the first day of April next following the calendar year in which the Agreement enters into force
source_title: Income Tax Department (India) law database: India-Lithuania DTAA with Notification No. 28/2012 (s.90) - Wayback copy (2013-07-24) of the official page

rates.quote: ( a ) 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the beneficial owner is a company (other than a partnership) which holds directly at least 10 per cent of the capital of the company paying the dividends;
( b ) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.

However, such interest may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the interest is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

However, such royalties or fees for technical services may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties or fees for technical services is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties or fees for technical services.

ppt.quote: [MLI Art. 7(1)] Notwithstanding any provisions of a Covered Tax Agreement, a benefit under the Covered Tax Agreement shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Covered Tax Agreement. || [Lithuania MLI position, Art. 7(17)(a)] 21 India Article 30(1)

notes: Agreement EIF 2012-07-10 (India Notification No. 28/2012); effective in India for WHT on income derived on/after 1 April 2013 (Lithuanian-side effective date in Art. 31(3)(b) not captured in the archived copy; presumably 1 January 2013 - unverified). MLI: Lithuania EIF 2019-01-01, India 2019-10-01; WHT effect in India from 1 April 2020 (India Art. 35(2)), in Lithuania from 1 January 2020 (map mli_wht_effective). MLI Art. 8 365-day holding period does NOT apply: Lithuania reserved the entirety of Art. 8 (Art. 8(3)(a)) although India notified Art. 10(2)(a). Lithuania did not choose SLOB (it chose Art. 7(4) only) -> India's SLOB does not apply; PPT applies; both notified treaty Art. 30(1) (main-purpose LOB) as existing provision. Interest exempt at source if derived and beneficially owned by the Government/political subdivision/local authority, Reserve Bank of India, Exim Bank of India, National Housing Bank, Bank of Lithuania, or other agreed wholly Government-owned financial institutions (Art. 11(3)) - not modelled. Royalty cap covers fees for technical services. No MFN clause on rates (Protocol only has an insurance-PE consultation clause).
unverified: Lithuanian-side effective date of the Agreement
Text is a 2013 archived copy; no amending protocol is known (map latest_protocol null)
